name: 3D crack propagation benchmark problem
description: We propose a full 3D benchmark problem for brittle fracture based on experiments as well as a validation in the context of phase-field models. The example consists of a series of four-point bending tests on graphite specimens with sharp V-notches at different inclination angles. This simple setup leads to a mixed mode (I + II + III) loading which results in complex yet stably reproducible crack surfaces. The proposed problem is well suited for benchmarking numerical methods for brittle fracture and allows for a quantitative comparison of failure loads and propagation paths as well as initiation angles and the fracture surface. For evaluation of the crack surfaces image-based 3D models of the fractured specimen are provided along with experimental and numerical results. In addition, measured failure loads and computed load-displacement curves are given. reputation: A well-known physics/engineering benchmark problem used to compare brittle fracture and phase-field simulation methods in 3D.
notes: Not an ML benchmark in the usual sense; evaluation is based on agreement with experimental failure loads, load-displacement curves, crack initiation angles, and crack propagation paths. Small, domain-specific benchmark with no standard single score.
